boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named campus spaces for focused work, collaborative projects, making, art, and reflection.

cards.title: Collaboration Studio
cards.subtitle: J. Paul Leonard Library, LIB 124
cards.notes: Bring a project group to the first-floor studio, use its computers or printers, and reserve a study room when you need a contained work session.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor library workspace built for collaborative study and practical tech tasks.
cards.evidence_claim: The Collaboration Studio has computers, printers, reservable study rooms, a peer-mentor help desk, and large tables for collaborative work.
cards.source_title: Centering students’ needs in reimagined spaces
cards.access_notes: Located on the first floor of J. Paul Leonard Library; study rooms are reservable.

cards.title: The Living Room
cards.subtitle: J. Paul Leonard Library, LIB 124C
cards.notes: Take a deliberate break between classes with a puzzle, craft, or leisure book, then return to the adjacent Collaboration Studio when it is time to work.
cards.short_summary: A daylight-filled library room set up for restorative breaks as well as quiet downtime.
cards.evidence_claim: The Living Room is attached to the Collaboration Studio and offers natural light, armchairs, puzzles, crafts, and leisure-reading books.
cards.source_title: Centering students’ needs in reimagined spaces
cards.access_notes: Located in LIB 124C, attached to the first-floor Collaboration Studio.

cards.title: Silent Study Room
cards.subtitle: J. Paul Leonard Library, LIB 41
cards.notes: Choose this ground-floor room for distraction-light reading or writing; plan to keep conversation, food, phones, and audio outside the room.
cards.short_summary: A designated silent library room for heads-down individual work.
cards.evidence_claim: The Silent Study Room is on the library ground floor, and talking, eating, phone use, and audio devices are not allowed there.
cards.source_title: Centering students’ needs in reimagined spaces
cards.access_notes: Ground floor; the library floor map identifies it as LIB 41.

cards.title: Digital Media Studio and MakerSpace
cards.subtitle: J. Paul Leonard Library, LIB 260
cards.notes: Use this second-floor studio when a class project needs 3D printing, VR, high-end computers, specialized software, scanning, or equipment checkout.
cards.short_summary: A hands-on media-production space with digital tools and equipment support.
cards.evidence_claim: The Digital Media Studio and MakerSpace supports SFSU projects with 3D printers, VR headsets, high-end computers, specialized software, scanning, and equipment checkout.
cards.access_notes: LIB 260 on the library’s second floor; the official page lists regular-semester hours.

cards.title: Special Collections & Archives Gallery
cards.subtitle: J. Paul Leonard Library, LIB 462
cards.notes: Stop by the fourth-floor gallery to spend time with the current exhibition, then check the library events page for related talks or gallery programs.
cards.short_summary: A fourth-floor exhibition gallery next to Special Collections & Archives.
cards.evidence_claim: The Special Collections Gallery is on the fourth floor beside the Special Collections & Archives Reading Room, and exhibitions are free and open to the campus community and public.
cards.access_notes: Fourth floor, adjacent to the Special Collections & Archives Reading Room.

cards.title: Special Collections & Archives Reading Room
cards.subtitle: J. Paul Leonard Library, LIB 460
cards.notes: Plan an archival-research visit when your topic calls for rare books or primary sources; contact Special Collections first if you need help preparing a request.
cards.short_summary: A fourth-floor reading room for working with rare books and primary-source material.
cards.evidence_claim: SFSU directs students seeking rare books and primary-source material to the Special Collections & Archives Reading Room on the library’s fourth floor.
cards.source_title: Information for Students | J. Paul Leonard Library
cards.access_notes: Fourth-floor LIB 460; contact Special Collections & Archives for research assistance or access questions.

cards.title: Quiet Study
cards.subtitle: J. Paul Leonard Library, LIB 485
cards.notes: Head to the fourth floor when you need a calmer reading or drafting block, and keep voices low so the shared quiet-study setting remains usable.
cards.short_summary: A designated fourth-floor quiet-study area among the library’s open stacks.
cards.evidence_claim: The library’s fourth floor is a quiet study area, and its floor map identifies Quiet Study in LIB 485.
cards.source_title: Floor Maps | J. Paul Leonard Library
cards.access_notes: Fourth floor; designated quiet areas require low voices and minimal talking.

cards.title: Garden of Remembrance
cards.subtitle: Between Burk Hall and the Fine Arts Building
cards.notes: Use the garden as a reflective pause on the way across campus, and read its memorial elements with attention to the history they commemorate.
cards.short_summary: A campus memorial garden honoring Japanese American incarceration and affected SF State students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Garden of Remembrance honors Japanese Americans incarcerated during World War II, including 19 SF State students, and is free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Visit the Garden | Fine Arts Gallery
cards.access_notes: Located between Burk Hall and the Fine Arts Building; east and west entrances are described by the gallery.

cards.title: Associated Students Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: Cesar Chavez Student Center, T-139
cards.notes: Check the exhibition schedule before visiting, then use a current show or reception as a starting point for conversation about artists and community issues.
cards.short_summary: A student-funded, student-staffed gallery presenting visual and interdisciplinary work.
cards.evidence_claim: Associated Students describes its Art Gallery as student-funded and student-staffed; it presents student, faculty, and professional work and hosts exhibits and events.
cards.access_notes: Located in the Student Center at T-139; consult the gallery’s current exhibition information before visiting.

cards.title: Events Room
cards.subtitle: J. Paul Leonard Library, LIB 121
cards.notes: Look at the library events calendar before crossing the quad; use a listed workshop, talk, or program as an easy way to connect coursework with campus life.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor library venue used for campus workshops, talks, and other programs.
cards.evidence_claim: The library identifies the Events Room as LIB 121 on the first floor and lists it as a frequent location for events and meetings.
cards.access_notes: LIB 121 on the first floor; availability changes when it is scheduled for events or meetings.
